Exported Animals Investigation

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Did you know thousands of our animals are exported every year - traded to zoos, sold as pets and enter into the meat market... We investigate where they really end up and what happens to them.

Unique Selling Point:
The illegal wildlife trade according to Interpol is a multibillion dollar industry, but sitting on top of it and arguably allowing it is the legal trade. All that’s required is a piece of paper from CITES and permits. This trade also allows wild animals to enter the pet trade, and if you check youtube, these animals are shown off as the proud property of pet owners world wide. So what is the cost to the animal when it comes to South Africa’s wildlife? 5 freedoms.
R600,000 for a cheetah cub – hand reared, it costs thousands per week to feed, needs lots of space to run and has expensive vet bills. But that doesn’t seem to bother those overseas intent on having a Cheetah – which is marketed like a “cat most like a dog” to those people who then get them as a pet.
These predators end up being kept in cages, in weather that it’s not used to, interacting and being treated like it’s human - eating beef, chicken or whatever is available – nothing like it’s natural habitat in South Africa.
How do they end up here? (Show Sheiks in the United Arab Emirates with Cheetah’s in their palaces, cheetah in snow etc) Smaragda from Ban Animal Trading will speak about this – she has just put together a report about the trade of animals and how they are exploited overseas. (Will be published end of this month) This is explosive report names the wildlife traders that are sending our animals into the pet trade. All that’s required is a permit from CITES to trade in animals - an import permit (vetinary permits) from the country of destination and export permit from South Africa (granted by environmental affairs – provincially – with a health certificate to certify all the health requirements are met). But this is a massive industry – and for some organizations the permits and way bills have revealed are making millions!
Although many of these facilities are known cub petting facilities there are some that stand out – especially those that claim to be rehabilitation or sanctuary facilities. Smargada can explain the differences. Sadly there is no law of what these are, and with cub petting fast becoming a “no-no” for tourists, are some facilities pretending to be something else?


Summary:
Take Hoedspruit Endangered Species Centre (according to 5 sources they are fake) they have a history of being a canned lion facility with Johann Roode leading the way – but when he died, his wife Lente took over and said changed everything all to promote the continuation of the cheetah species. Their aim was to rehabilitate wild animals, and also breed cheetah captivity and then release them. But this say numerous people is a lie told to the public. Doesn’t want anyone to know about them selling the animals – they claim to be a rehabilitation facility – which means no breeding of animals, and releases back into the wild – but its clear that they are not that. State vet speaks to this very well!
It can be assimilated to a Puppy mill but for Cheetah. A cheetah will only breed every two years in the wild, but here they breed 2-3 times a year – the moment take its cubs away it can come into estrous again.
Source 1:Russia – Dr. Steinmann – State Vet (hidden identity) - Hoedspruit
1. There has not been one release since they’ve known them. That’s since 2012. never released in 6 years – hyena was released that was wild.
2. TB – how they were under quarantine and the dangers with animals that have tb- can ALSO SPREAD TO HUMANS. Lente was afraid this would hurt the business as ppl want to ride elephants etc at Jabulani which is also on Kapama
3. Hand rearing of animals to be pets
4. Lente herself – she’s a racist, tells everyone what to do – only in it for money
5. Not hand reared – cubs grow up with mom…
6. Baby elephant taken from kruger – mapani - they are teaching him commands and raising him probably to go to jabulani - yet it's from the kruger. The kruger has a zero intervention policy.
7. Why 10 cheetah going to a zoo like to china? Or 9 to canada?
8. Some shipments don’t have permits
9. Rhino’s that have been poached or were calves and their mothers were poached are taken away and never put back in wild


Further information:
Source 2: Charlie Penny – she was a volunteer (2016 nov-2017 oct) She now works for the Black Mamas anti-poaching unit (hidden identity) - hoedspruit
1. Talk about the way the animals are treated as a commodity - inbreeding with king cheetah – money making
2. All hand reared, and when the animals die they are put into the museum
3. Rhino’s were not released – horns are shaved off – cut off
4. Lente is con-woman
5. None have ever been released
6. History of facility as a canned lion hunt
7. Wild dogs – ripping apart the other animals – against vets instructions they killed each other (from other packs)
8. Treated the birds of prey was cruel – because they have a bataleur and a vulture in a tiny cage together and they should be released
9. Has lots of photos of interactions
Source 3: In Pretoria: Inge Dekker –volunteer (2008-2012) (hidden identity) - pretoria
1. She was there when two cheetah were released (they were the only animals released), and the animals were recaptured and put back in their cages.
2. Lente was near bankrupt and that’s why she decided to start selling the animals
3. Thinks it’s a fake facility – nothing about the animals – only about lente and her reputation.
4. Says they hand reared all the animals and its not a rehab facility
5. She says she has lots of other examples - is looking for her photos

Source 4: Louise De Waal– on camera (will speak on camera) - pretoria
This is puppy mill – only with cheetah.
recorded lente audio-- telling her about 150 cheetah on property!!!– and that she’s selling them as pets etc Very nice stuff – but we get lente on camera telling us as well.
Christo – he will only confirm things for me – not willing to be interviewed – but confirms they sell them and a couple of other things too.
video – undercover showing lente talking about her raising cheetah’s as pets – taking them away from their mother and keeps them at her house – wants to sell a rhino so guy can have one in his garden, ppl want them younger than 6 months. keeps breeding them.
Video: of the facility undercover – sasha goes undercover – they tell her they never send to zoos, badmouth other parks, they tell her they released 200 animals – but none have been released since 2008 – of if they have they were recaptured. Saw the king cheetah (they are inbred) use them to make money.
Interview Smaragda – she’s got lots on them and on Christa Saayman. Has all the permits from the airport – and the way bills – they have prices too. So HESC has sent a number of animals overseas – to zoos and as pets.
We potentially need to go to:
Mystic monkeys – Christa Saayman - now they openly say they export etc –but they are the ones doing the business for lente – doing the dirty work and finding the clients for pets. So we will include information on her as well – might have to go up there and video her facility too. It’s about an hour and a half from joburg in north Pretoria.
So I have interviewed Vince from protrack for Kathi's story on crooks corner - he was excellent - very good - got him teaching his people.
REGARDING THE STORY:
I think we should use Derek - get him to call and not giver her too much time - she is also in Pretoria and often takes the baby cheetah with her back to pretoria illegally. (no permits) we should ask her and tell her we would come the next day or something.
So i have interviewed Dr. Steinmann and Charlie Penny already - but obviously we would need a presenter. We would need drone visuals of kapama - there are lots of video's online of roode too - also animal interactions etc.
I think i should see whose available up here to shoot for me and who can keep quiet about it - its a small town, so its been sooooo hard to hide me being around Dr. Steinmann! Seriously hard! Anyway, i think it's strong :)
We have lots of video of Roode :) so happy about that!

Press Release:


Cheetah Cheater – The Wildlife Export Trade
Every year thousands of wild animals are exported out of South Africa and traded to zoos, sold as pets or simply disappear abroad – potentially ending up in meat markets. High on the demand list is one of Africa’s favourite short-distance sprinters – the cheetah. Marketed as the “cat most like a dog”, a King Cheetah can cost up to R1.5 million a pop. Raising a cheetah cub as a pet can lead to its death as its diet is too specialised to easily be accommodated. But that doesn’t put off international buyers. Interpol says the illegal wildlife trade is a multi-billion-dollar industry, but overlaying, and probably supporting it, is the legal trade. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


ACCORDING TO INTERPOL THE ILLEGAL WILDLIFE TRADE IS A MULTIBILLION DOLLAR INDUSTRY, BUT SITTING ON TOP OF IT AND ARGUABLY ALLOWING IT IS THE LEGAL TRADE. ALL THAT’S REQUIRED IS A PIECE OF PAPER FROM CITES AND PERMITS.
In 2015 Carte Blanche exposed the animal trade; first how exotic pets like tigers were popping up in suburbia. And then how these pets were smuggled into South Africa where they have no rights in comparison to our indigenous wildlife.
AND NOW A NEW REPORT SHOWING THAT AT LEAST 5,000 ANIMALS HAVE BEEN EXPORTED TO THE EAST IN THE LAST 4 YEARS.
The joint report was compiled by two animal rights organizations: It reveals where our captive bred animals are exported to. Ban Animal Trading’s Smaragda Louw objects to the breeding and sale of animals and after gaining access to thousands of permits she traveled to Bangladesh, Pakistan, Vietnam and China to see where our animals end up...
SMARAGDA: A trader in Pakistan says he’s on the sixth floor of this building, I get there and it's a crumbling ruin. So where are the animals?
This trade is controlled by governing body CITES, which monitors the international trade in Endangered Species. All permits must state the number and species, and the import permit from the destination country must be issued before the export permit. CITES 1 listed animals are most threatened with extinction, and therefore may not be traded for commercial purposes. Whereas CITES II listed animals can be traded.
Derek: So where are the loopholes?
Some animals are CITES I listed animals. But if the facility where you breed them is listed with CITES then you can sell them as CITES II listed animals for commercial purpose.
They're a trade organization. We need an organization in place that actually protects the animals.We export more than 300 giraffes to one zoo.
Derek: 300?
S: More than 300. I get there and they are 16.
Where the other 284 giraffes went from this Asian zoo is unknown - but the report says potentially exported animals are sold on into the pet trade or meat markets.
CITES acknowledge that their policies need updating, as no framework exists. All CITES registered zoos can legally trade in animals but they’re not meant to profit from that trade.
The report concentrates on breeding facilities of which South Africa has 50. One of these is the Hoedspruit Endangered Species Center - or HESC. Owner Lente Roode prides herself as one of three facilities reintroducing captive bred cheetah into the wild. This is ‘lovers lane’ where over 100 breeding Cheetah are kept…
UPSOUND: We breed them here and release them back out into the wild.
Derek: HESC at Hoedspruit, do they come into the report?
S: Yes they do. And not in a very good way because we would expect a sanctuary not to trade in animals.
Our investigation began in 2018. We interviewed several insiders like “Blue” who claimed HESC is like a puppy mill for Cheetah.
Blue: So the cubs are taken away from their moms and hand raised. Then they’re sold. If the cubs are taken away, they go on cycle again. You can have more than 1 litter a year.
“Blue” said HESC unethically sold Cheetah as pets.
Blue: I know of 4 sent to Spain, cheetahs that were kept at Mrs Roode’s house. They have to be younger than 6 months, otherwise the clients are not interested in buying them.
Now “Blue” says HESC is under severe financial strain.
Blue: They have a surplus of cheetahs which now they have to take care off. They are considering to euthanize 18 cheetahs.
Carte Blanche visited HESC which is located in Limpopo, and met Roode’s tame king cheetah…
P: Most King cheetahs are so severely inbred purely because of the demand...they'll pay big bucks they'll pay a hundred thousand US dollars.
Cheetah expert and veterinarian Dr Peter Caldwell has been rewilding Cheetah for 18 years.
P: A lot of breeding these facilities say they do it because the only way they can get funding is if they are conservation minded That is SO not the case.
THERE’S A VIEW THAT CHEETAH MAKE GOOD PETS, THAT YOU CAN DISCIPLINE THEM AND HOUSE TRAIN THEM LIKE A DOG AND THERES A MASSIVE INTERNATIONAL DEMAND FOR CAPTIVE BRED CUBS…
Derek: We’ve seen Cheetah at palaces in the middle east?
P: This guy imported a king cheetah for his daughters’ 21st. They were feeding this cheetah donuts in the palace, and this animal was just showing signs of nutritional deficiency and what these people do, is they just buy another animal.
Derek: Lenta it seems that you have exported cheetah which have been used as pets?
L: Not many...
Derek: You sent Four Cheetah to Spain in 2017 (yes) for photography?
L: Yeah
Derek: Is that the right thing to do?
L: I think so. It was a nice place he did photography so I think that the animals were happy,
Derek: But lenta to be fair you're not sure about the fate of all the Cheetah that you export?
L: Yeah that's true. Yeah.
The Endangered wildlife trust or EWT’s Vincent Van Der Merwe runs their Cheetah rewilding project.
V: There is certainly no conservation value to taking a cheetah and making it a pet, that is purely for human entertainment. We in South Africa have a growing wild cheetah population, I think the idea of holding cheetah's in cages is becoming outdated.
Cheetah’s have specialized dietary requirements.
P: Ideal milk is Mom's milk. I get multiple cases of cheetah cubs with 13 bone fractures.
D: And have you lost a lot of young Cheetah?
L: Ya, Fifty.
Derek: fifty?
L: And then it was always, kidney failure. Many years ago we developed a supplement for the Cheetahs, I cannot afford giving them venison, so they eat meat from a feedlot that I get...I only found the solution after 50.
Derek: Doesn't that upset you?
L: Very much.(she laughs?) makes you depressed.
SOME BREEDERS CLAIM THAT THEY ARE EXPANDING THE GENE POOL BY REWILDING CAPTIVE-BRED CHEETAH BUT ITS AN EXTREMELY DELICATE, LENGTHY AND COSTLY PROCESS.
Roode claims she’s released almost 100 Cheetah. But EWT says HESC has only had one successful release.
A successful release is where Individuals pass their genetics on next generation. then you can consider that reintroduction to be successful.
Looking at hesc, do you know how many successful rewildings they've had?
Unfortunately these reintroductions were not successful.
Derek: How many Cheetah have you successfully rewilded?
L: 96.
Derek: Some organizations are saying there's only been one successful rewilding?
L: Yeah they don't know what I'm doing. Not all of them were successful. If there's a problem then I bring them back.
HESC later claimed they define a successful release as a Cheetah that can hunt, therefore they’ve had 68 successful releases.
D: Are you planning to euthanize, I think it's 18 Cheetah?
L: I've got 18 old animals that cannot be bred anymore and they're too old to release. And I was thinking of having like a retirement village, but with this Corona Virus I cannot afford this. They were coalition of males and I thought it's better for them to be released it's a second chance.
D: So instead of euthanizing them you released them?
L: Yeah.
D: And are they surviving?
No they didn't.
Roode had to recapture them after they attacked a child. She’s assured us the Cheetah won’t be euthanized.
D: Lenta there was a child attack last month and apparently by one of the Cheetah that had been released.
L: It was people who worked here and they didn't close the gate. The child is fine now. It was not that serious. Now there’s a case that I'm facing that I've released cheetahs without a permit.
Derek: Some people say that in many ways HESC is like the equivalent of a puppy mill?
L: Oh wow that's bad to hear something something like this.
D: Have you got to the point where really you will have to get rid of more Cheetah?
L: I must do it, ja, I've got too many cheetahs.
Another breeder is Christa Saayman, owner of Mystic Monkeys and Feathers in limpopo. She’s a well known wildlife trader also featured in the report after exporting chimpanzees last year.
S: The facility that those chimpanzees went to hadn't even been built. So they were kept in these like cages for almost six months. It's a massive trading business of wild animals - on her website it says that she's a sanctuary. And she even asks for donations. Why?
Saayman exported 10 Cheetah for Roode worth R275,000 each.
S: And we also found some problems with that specific export for example the import permit was issued after the export permit. And in terms of cites that then means that that export should never have taken place.
We showed Roode examples of where Cheetahs are kept at the zoo.
Derek: The conditions look dismal?
really?
Derek: I'll show you what I've got. I mean there's no grass there. I mean they're just in a small encampment.
Lente: Can I have a picture of it?
Derek: Sure. (hands over)
Lente: Yeah they're small.
Roode says the Zoo supplied her with this aerial photo - and Saayman sent these.
Lente: This is very upsetting, very upsetting.
We visited Saayman’s Zoo which controversially allows the petting of cubs like this one...
Employee: it’s very difficult for the parents to take care of the young one, they can kill.
An employee says the cubs parents still breed at 13 years old.
Producer: Are they still going to mate?
Employee: Yes.
Producer: How many cubs do the tigers have?
Employee: They make four at a time. Four. .Three. Six. The other time we had Six.
Saayman has exported 60 tigers overseas averaging at R120,000 per cat and spends R2.5 million a month on upkeep. She explained that the Cheetah permits were in order, as the dates were amended because the import permit expired.
Saayman: I don’t say abuse animals at all. I’ve got rare animals, so what my mission in life is to breed for our nation for the kids. There’s no zoo in the world that can sustain or make any profit if you don’t breed and sell. I was accused of smuggling chimpanzees. I was only the agent. You must see that enclosure, it’s out of this world. This Ban Animal Trading they just assume and think you’re a crook.
How do we know that this report is really unbiased?
S: Our reports are going to be, ‘these are the reasons why you shouldn't be doing this.’ But, we have proof for every single reason we put out there.
SO IS NOW POSSIBLY THE TIME TO RETHINK THE EXPORT OF OUR WILDLIFE TO UNCERTAIN DESTINATIONS OVERSEAS?
D: So it sounds like you're not truly happy about exporting captive bred Cheetah?
Lenta: No no.
D: But why have you done it for so long
L: Money.
What just to make a profit?
L: no, not to profit. I didn't get one cent for myself. I feel there is a time maybe that I should go smaller or close down.
And stop exporting?
Lenta: And stop exporting. 13:09

Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 11 June 2020 Press Release: Cheetah Cheater – The Wildlife Export Trade Every year thousands of wild animals are exported out of South Africa and traded to zoos, sold as pets or simply disappear abroad – potentially ending up in meat markets. High on the demand list is one of Africa’s favourite short-distance sprinters – the cheetah. Marketed as the “cat most like a dog”, a King Cheetah can cost up to R1.5 million a pop. Raising a cheetah cub as a pet can lead to its death as its diet is too specialised to easily be accommodated. But that doesn’t put off international buyers. Interpol says the illegal wildlife trade is a multi-billion-dollar industry, but overlaying, and probably supporting it, is the legal trade. Carte Blanche investigates. Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein | Presenter: Derek Watts Script: ACCORDING TO INTERPOL THE ILLEGAL WILDLIFE TRADE IS A MULTIBILLION DOLLAR INDUSTRY, BUT SITTING ON TOP OF IT AND ARGUABLY ALLOWING IT IS THE LEGAL TRADE. ALL THAT’S REQUIRED IS A PIECE OF PAPER FROM CITES AND PERMITS. In 2015 Carte Blanche exposed the animal trade; first how exotic pets like tigers were popping up in suburbia. And then how these pets were smuggled into South Africa where they have no rights in comparison to our indigenous wildlife. AND NOW A NEW REPORT SHOWING THAT AT LEAST 5,000 ANIMALS HAVE BEEN EXPORTED TO THE EAST IN THE LAST 4 YEARS. The joint report was compiled by two animal rights organizations: It reveals where our captive bred animals are exported to. Ban Animal Trading’s Smaragda Louw objects to the breeding and sale of animals and after gaining access to thousands of permits she traveled to Bangladesh, Pakistan, Vietnam and China to see where our animals end up... SMARAGDA: A trader in Pakistan says he’s on the sixth floor of this building, I get there and it's a crumbling ruin. So where are the animals? This trade is controlled by governing body CITES, which monitors the international trade in Endangered Species. All permits must state the number and species, and the import permit from the destination country must be issued before the export permit. CITES 1 listed animals are most threatened with extinction, and therefore may not be traded for commercial purposes. Whereas CITES II listed animals can be traded. Derek: So where are the loopholes? Some animals are CITES I listed animals. But if the facility where you breed them is listed with CITES then you can sell them as CITES II listed animals for commercial purpose. They're a trade organization. We need an organization in place that actually protects the animals.We export more than 300 giraffes to one zoo. Derek: 300? S: More than 300. I get there and they are 16. Where the other 284 giraffes went from this Asian zoo is unknown - but the report says potentially exported animals are sold on into the pet trade or meat markets. CITES acknowledge that their policies need updating, as no framework exists. All CITES registered zoos can legally trade in animals but they’re not meant to profit from that trade. The report concentrates on breeding facilities of which South Africa has 50. One of these is the Hoedspruit Endangered Species Center - or HESC. Owner Lente Roode prides herself as one of three facilities reintroducing captive bred cheetah into the wild. This is ‘lovers lane’ where over 100 breeding Cheetah are kept… UPSOUND: We breed them here and release them back out into the wild. Derek: HESC at Hoedspruit, do they come into the report? S: Yes they do. And not in a very good way because we would expect a sanctuary not to trade in animals. Our investigation began in 2018. We interviewed several insiders like “Blue” who claimed HESC is like a puppy mill for Cheetah. Blue: So the cubs are taken away from their moms and hand raised. Then they’re sold. If the cubs are taken away, they go on cycle again. You can have more than 1 litter a year. “Blue” said HESC unethically sold Cheetah as pets. Blue: I know of 4 sent to Spain, cheetahs that were kept at Mrs Roode’s house. They have to be younger than 6 months, otherwise the clients are not interested in buying them. Now “Blue” says HESC is under severe financial strain. Blue: They have a surplus of cheetahs which now they have to take care off. They are considering to euthanize 18 cheetahs. Carte Blanche visited HESC which is located in Limpopo, and met Roode’s tame king cheetah… P: Most King cheetahs are so severely inbred purely because of the demand...they'll pay big bucks they'll pay a hundred thousand US dollars. Cheetah expert and veterinarian Dr Peter Caldwell has been rewilding Cheetah for 18 years. P: A lot of breeding these facilities say they do it because the only way they can get funding is if they are conservation minded That is SO not the case. THERE’S A VIEW THAT CHEETAH MAKE GOOD PETS, THAT YOU CAN DISCIPLINE THEM AND HOUSE TRAIN THEM LIKE A DOG AND THERES A MASSIVE INTERNATIONAL DEMAND FOR CAPTIVE BRED CUBS… Derek: We’ve seen Cheetah at palaces in the middle east? P: This guy imported a king cheetah for his daughters’ 21st. They were feeding this cheetah donuts in the palace, and this animal was just showing signs of nutritional deficiency and what these people do, is they just buy another animal. Derek: Lenta it seems that you have exported cheetah which have been used as pets? L: Not many... Derek: You sent Four Cheetah to Spain in 2017 (yes) for photography? L: Yeah Derek: Is that the right thing to do? L: I think so. It was a nice place he did photography so I think that the animals were happy, Derek: But lenta to be fair you're not sure about the fate of all the Cheetah that you export? L: Yeah that's true. Yeah. The Endangered wildlife trust or EWT’s Vincent Van Der Merwe runs their Cheetah rewilding project. V: There is certainly no conservation value to taking a cheetah and making it a pet, that is purely for human entertainment. We in South Africa have a growing wild cheetah population, I think the idea of holding cheetah's in cages is becoming outdated. Cheetah’s have specialized dietary requirements. P: Ideal milk is Mom's milk. I get multiple cases of cheetah cubs with 13 bone fractures. D: And have you lost a lot of young Cheetah? L: Ya, Fifty. Derek: fifty? L: And then it was always, kidney failure. Many years ago we developed a supplement for the Cheetahs, I cannot afford giving them venison, so they eat meat from a feedlot that I get...I only found the solution after 50. Derek: Doesn't that upset you? L: Very much.(she laughs?) makes you depressed. SOME BREEDERS CLAIM THAT THEY ARE EXPANDING THE GENE POOL BY REWILDING CAPTIVE-BRED CHEETAH BUT ITS AN EXTREMELY DELICATE, LENGTHY AND COSTLY PROCESS. Roode claims she’s released almost 100 Cheetah. But EWT says HESC has only had one successful release. A successful release is where Individuals pass their genetics on next generation. then you can consider that reintroduction to be successful. Looking at hesc, do you know how many successful rewildings they've had? Unfortunately these reintroductions were not successful. Derek: How many Cheetah have you successfully rewilded? L: 96. Derek: Some organizations are saying there's only been one successful rewilding? L: Yeah they don't know what I'm doing. Not all of them were successful. If there's a problem then I bring them back. HESC later claimed they define a successful release as a Cheetah that can hunt, therefore they’ve had 68 successful releases. D: Are you planning to euthanize, I think it's 18 Cheetah? L: I've got 18 old animals that cannot be bred anymore and they're too old to release. And I was thinking of having like a retirement village, but with this Corona Virus I cannot afford this. They were coalition of males and I thought it's better for them to be released it's a second chance. D: So instead of euthanizing them you released them? L: Yeah. D: And are they surviving? No they didn't. Roode had to recapture them after they attacked a child. She’s assured us the Cheetah won’t be euthanized. D: Lenta there was a child attack last month and apparently by one of the Cheetah that had been released. L: It was people who worked here and they didn't close the gate. The child is fine now. It was not that serious. Now there’s a case that I'm facing that I've released cheetahs without a permit. Derek: Some people say that in many ways HESC is like the equivalent of a puppy mill? L: Oh wow that's bad to hear something something like this. D: Have you got to the point where really you will have to get rid of more Cheetah? L: I must do it, ja, I've got too many cheetahs. Another breeder is Christa Saayman, owner of Mystic Monkeys and Feathers in limpopo. She’s a well known wildlife trader also featured in the report after exporting chimpanzees last year. S: The facility that those chimpanzees went to hadn't even been built. So they were kept in these like cages for almost six months. It's a massive trading business of wild animals - on her website it says that she's a sanctuary. And she even asks for donations. Why? Saayman exported 10 Cheetah for Roode worth R275,000 each. S: And we also found some problems with that specific export for example the import permit was issued after the export permit. And in terms of cites that then means that that export should never have taken place. We showed Roode examples of where Cheetahs are kept at the zoo. Derek: The conditions look dismal? really? Derek: I'll show you what I've got. I mean there's no grass there. I mean they're just in a small encampment. Lente: Can I have a picture of it? Derek: Sure. (hands over) Lente: Yeah they're small. Roode says the Zoo supplied her with this aerial photo - and Saayman sent these. Lente: This is very upsetting, very upsetting. We visited Saayman’s Zoo which controversially allows the petting of cubs like this one... Employee: it’s very difficult for the parents to take care of the young one, they can kill. An employee says the cubs parents still breed at 13 years old. Producer: Are they still going to mate? Employee: Yes. Producer: How many cubs do the tigers have? Employee: They make four at a time. Four. .Three. Six. The other time we had Six. Saayman has exported 60 tigers overseas averaging at R120,000 per cat and spends R2.5 million a month on upkeep. She explained that the Cheetah permits were in order, as the dates were amended because the import permit expired. Saayman: I don’t say abuse animals at all. I’ve got rare animals, so what my mission in life is to breed for our nation for the kids. There’s no zoo in the world that can sustain or make any profit if you don’t breed and sell. I was accused of smuggling chimpanzees. I was only the agent. You must see that enclosure, it’s out of this world. This Ban Animal Trading they just assume and think you’re a crook. How do we know that this report is really unbiased? S: Our reports are going to be, ‘these are the reasons why you shouldn't be doing this.’ But, we have proof for every single reason we put out there. SO IS NOW POSSIBLY THE TIME TO RETHINK THE EXPORT OF OUR WILDLIFE TO UNCERTAIN DESTINATIONS OVERSEAS? D: So it sounds like you're not truly happy about exporting captive bred Cheetah? Lenta: No no. D: But why have you done it for so long L: Money. What just to make a profit? L: no, not to profit. I didn't get one cent for myself. I feel there is a time maybe that I should go smaller or close down. And stop exporting? Lenta: And stop exporting. 13:09

metadata.Unique Selling Point: The illegal wildlife trade according to Interpol is a multibillion dollar industry, but sitting on top of it and arguably allowing it is the legal trade. All that’s required is a piece of paper from CITES and permits. This trade also allows wild animals to enter the pet trade, and if you check youtube, these animals are shown off as the proud property of pet owners world wide. So what is the cost to the animal when it comes to South Africa’s wildlife? 5 freedoms. R600,000 for a cheetah cub – hand reared, it costs thousands per week to feed, needs lots of space to run and has expensive vet bills. But that doesn’t seem to bother those overseas intent on having a Cheetah – which is marketed like a “cat most like a dog” to those people who then get them as a pet. These predators end up being kept in cages, in weather that it’s not used to, interacting and being treated like it’s human - eating beef, chicken or whatever is available – nothing like it’s natural habitat in South Africa. How do they end up here? (Show Sheiks in the United Arab Emirates with Cheetah’s in their palaces, cheetah in snow etc) Smaragda from Ban Animal Trading will speak about this – she has just put together a report about the trade of animals and how they are exploited overseas. (Will be published end of this month) This is explosive report names the wildlife traders that are sending our animals into the pet trade. All that’s required is a permit from CITES to trade in animals - an import permit (vetinary permits) from the country of destination and export permit from South Africa (granted by environmental affairs – provincially – with a health certificate to certify all the health requirements are met). But this is a massive industry – and for some organizations the permits and way bills have revealed are making millions! Although many of these facilities are known cub petting facilities there are some that stand out – especially those that claim to be rehabilitation or sanctuary facilities. Smargada can explain the differences. Sadly there is no law of what these are, and with cub petting fast becoming a “no-no” for tourists, are some facilities pretending to be something else?
